nearly 3 km duplicated edge geometry and failed QA despite reasonable local raster proximity

limitations: This is derived geometry reconstructed from the organizer's georeferenceable raster, not an organizer GPX or participant GPX.
The current organizer material retains a legacy 13 km map/profile while the modern event is marketed as about 14 km; exact year-to-year course identity is therefore not asserted.
The 2023 participant watch distance of 13.67 km is an independent plausibility observation, not a calibration target for route length.
Participant evidence is used to choose route direction because her race note places Hallamölla 4.5 km from the finish; the selected raster topology independently yields 4.524 km.
OSM is not used as the authoritative geometry where its graph conflicts with the organizer raster topology.
The 14.249 km raster-derived geometry is superseded. Its QA/provenance metadata is retained, but active route files were removed to prevent accidental runtime use.
superseded_reason: Visual inspection against real map context showed systematic corridor displacement. The preferred working hypothesis is now a 13.472 km Hallamölla splice recipe derived from Trail 21/22 2022-2024, pending authentic participant/organizer GPX.

replacement_reference.rationale: Use the verified Trail 21/22 2022-2024 geometry to Hallamölla, remove the eastern loop between two nearly identical Hallamölla passages, then continue on the same verified geometry to finish.

superseded_geometry_retention.recovery: Exact superseded route/candidate bytes remain recoverable from Git history if needed for audit.
